notes.title: THE JUNE PLAYTEST HAS ENDED
notes.content: [p]Hello, everyone! Thank you very, very much for joining us for the past few days. I hope you had an amazing time playing Shadows of Chroma Tower. To our returning players: thank you for sticking with us. And to all the new faces: welcome to the Tower![/p][p][/p][h2][b]What Is Our Takeaway?[/b][/h2][p]This shorter playtest was meant to evaluate the general direction our newly developed content was headed into - the endgame loop, the Invoker, Titan's Folly. We are quite happy with the results and are more confident than ever that this "traditional ARPG" power fantasy and game loop is indeed viable - both from a first person perspective and in an extraction context. [/p][h2][b]What's Next?[/b][/h2][p]We've been running playtests in quick succession from one another for a while now, but our next iteration will take a while longer to develop. Here is what we'll be working on in the following months: [/p][list][*][p][b]Skill Trees[/b] - one for each class, branching out into different specializations, vastly diversifying the ways to play and introducing new passive and active skills for everyone.[/p][/*][*][p][b]The First 10-Player Raid[/b] - you'll finally get to fight the Chromatic Abomination everyone is always asking about.[/p][/*][*][p][b]The Judgement fo the Titaness[/b] - a tower defense-like event within Titan's Folly, a sibling event to the Cursed Forge.[/p][/*][*][p][b]The Chromatic Trials[/b] - a coliseum-style roguelike gamemode that's part of the endgame loop.[/p][/*][*][p][b]The Immortal of Justice[/b] - the second summonable boss that resides within Titan's Folly.[/p][/*][/list][p]And of course, that’s just the new content. We’ve still got a mountain of work ahead on balancing, polish, and bug fixes - and that’ll take up a good chunk of our time as well. [/p][p][/p][p]Thanks again for playing, sharing your feedback, and being part of this journey! ːsteamhappyː[/p]

notes.title: PLAYTEST ANNOUNCEMENT - New Class, New Biome and More!
notes.content: [p][/p][previewyoutube="e_gQNBA_4gQ;full"][/previewyoutube][p][b]It's time again, everyone! Our next playtest is coming soon, here are SOME of the new features waiting for you:[/b][/p][h2][b]🪝New Class - The Invoker[/b][/h2][list][*][p][b]THE INVOKER[/b] arrives from the harsh North, drawn by whispers of glory within the Tower. Masters of afflictions, Invokers twist ailments to both bolster allies and unravel enemies.[/p][/*][*][p]Invokers bring with them [b]FLAILS AND CHAINMAIL ARMOR[/b], allowing them to stay relatively mobile and position themselves strategically within the battlefield without compromising too much protection.[/p][/*][/list][h2][b]🗺️New Biome - Titan's Folly[/b][/h2][list][*][p][b]TITAN'S FOLLY[/b] is now playable! You'll find new enemies with entirely new attack patterns and their own resistances and weaknesses within the land of the fallen titans.[/p][/*][*][p]For this playtest, matchmaking will randomly place you in Titan’s Folly or The Monastery (50/50 split with 3 map variants per biome). This is a temporary setup while we evaluate the impact of map randomness. Let us know what you think.[/p][/*][/list][h2][b]👹The First Boss - Immortal of Devotion[/b][/h2][list][*][p]The first [b]SUMMONABLE BOSS[/b] can be found within the halls of the Monastery [i](and, for now, within Titan's Folly as well while we finish its own summonable boss)[/i].[/p][/*][*][p][b]THE CHROMATIST ORDER[/b], having spread its presence all throughout the Tower and having been responsible for over 65% of the defeated minions of The Archmage in Goldwheat's last expedition, has made itself a target. [b]THE IMMORTAL OF DEVOTION[/b] has been summoned to wipe out all devouts from His dominion.[/p][list][*][p]The Tower [b]slowly corrupts[/b] those that ascend it, no matter whether they seek to attain power or to banish the Tower. The strongest beings who fall to the corruption are assimilated by the Tower and turned into one of the Archmage’s **Immortals**.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Immortals[/b] embody a twisted version of the corrupted being’s original ideals, often spreading them to servants of the Tower under their command.[/p][/*][*][p]They function as gatekeepers to the Tower’s deeper realms and powers. The Tower uses them to ensure that only those [b]worthy and thoroughly corrupted[/b] - those who are already claimed or in the process of being so - may proceed.[/p][/*][*][p]You may consider defeating [b]THE IMMORTAL OF DEVOTION[/b] the most notable feat for this playtest, but know that summonable bosses represent just the beginning of the endgame we have planned ahead.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][h2][b]🗼The Beginning of the End(game)[/b][/h2][list][*][p]With this playtest, we seek to test out the [b]very early stages of the players' endgame loop[/b] - that is to say, the gameplay loop that happens beyond Prismatic difficulty.[/p][/*][*][p][b]The Cursed Forge and Lairs[/b] have been revamped to adequately represent the first couple of steps players take in order to gear up to face challenges beyond the Prismatic difficulty. [/p][/*][*][p]Our aforementioned [b]first summonable boss[/b] has been introduced as the midway step between those two activities and the upcoming 10-player raids.[/p][/*][*][p]Legendary and Unique gear, lustrous runes and item socketing have been "redistributed" with these new activities in mind.[/p][/*][*][p]While players may farm the necessary resources from just Lairs and The Cursed Forge for now, we will introduce two new activities to this phase of the endgame loop in the near future:[/p][list][*][p][b]The Chromatic Trials[/b] - a high-intensity coliseum gamemode for parties of 3 that rewards maximizing your team's combat performance. This will be a separate gamemode like Lairs.[/p][/*][*][p][b]The Judgment of the Titaness[/b] - a tower-defense style event within Titan's Folly that will reward players looking to take their skill tree to the next level. You may think of this as a "sibling activity" to the Cursed Forge.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p]This playtest will go from [b]June 20th to June 22nd (Friday through Sunday)[/b]. Drop and crafting rates will be modified to account for the limited playtime, but we still expect getting to the endgame to be a challenge.[/p][p]See you in the Tower![/p]

notes.title: ✨ PLAYTEST STARTING NOW ✨
notes.content:
"Shadows of Chroma Tower Playtest" should now be available on your Steam Library to download.

We have made a TON of changes in the past couple of months. 
Here are the FULL patch notes:
https://doubledashstu.notion.site/soctpatchnotes

This playtest will last until April 13th. We hope you have a great time!

[u][b]Patch Highlights:
[/b][/u]

[b]New Features:
[/b]
[list]
[*] Factions & Territories
[*] Socketing and Runes
[*] Reforging
[*] Cursed Forge
[*] New Mini-Boss.
[*] Two new modules and 12 new Monastery variants
[*] New consumable
[*] Players may now reconnect to ongoing matches if their game crashes or their connection is lost.
[*] Image Settings
[/list]

[b]Major Changes:
[/b]
[list]
[*] Trios have been enabled! Players can now play with up to two other friends in the same party.
[*] Overhauled player progression speed - this is to account for the longer playtest period of 9 days compared to the previous 2 days. We intend to slow down player progression a bit further than what it is before we release in Early Access in the future.
[*] Major performance and networking improvements
[*] Escape Totems now spawn 1 portal for each party member alive, rather than just one overall.
[*] Players no longer lose their inventories when leaving the lobby. They still lose their inventories when leaving a match, of course.
[/list]

[b]General Changes and Improvements:
[/b]
[list]
[*] New movement and attack animations for several AI enemies.
[*] Currency and material costs, such as seen on crafting recipes, now display [owned resources]/[cost resources].
[*] Item tooltips now display attributes' composite value when inspected with [alt], such as Weapon Damage displaying [Base Damage + Bonus from Attribute Scaling].
[*] Added new adjustable keybindings: weapon selection (1, 2, 3) and skill and elixir use (Q, E and V).
[*] Cursed Chests now highlight its last few enemies on the player's screen and on their minimap. (No longer hunting that pesky last hidden Kobold!)
[*] Crafting tooltips now display perk information and attribute scaling.
[*] Doors will now interrupt player interactions when opened and closed.
[/list]

Access the full patch notes for fixes, balance changes, smaller improvements and more details on the list above.

notes.title: PLAYTEST ANNOUNCEMENT - APRIL 4TH
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=g3sV-0-hlbg;full][/previewyoutube]
[u][b][h1]PLAYTEST ANNOUNCEMENT: APRIL 4TH, 10 A.M. GMT-3[/h1][/b][/u]
Gather your allies and sharpen your blades - Goldwheat has split into two major factions and it's up to you to decide who rises to power!

[u][b][h2]Choose Your Side[/h2][/b][/u]
At the start of the playtest, [b]players will have to align with one of the two major factions[/b] vying for control of Chroma Tower. Each faction offers unique benefits and has their own agenda.
[list]
[*] [b]The Grey Fellowship[/b] - They believe the Tower is a [b]curse[/b], a source of corruption that has shattered Goldwheat’s fertile lands and attracted nothing but [b]greed and ruin[/b]. The Grey seek to study the Tower, undo its influence, and restore Goldwheat to its former glory. Their leaders - [b]court scholars and knights[/b] - fear that no amount of magic or treasure is worth the growing threat the Tower poses to the world itself.
[*] [b]The Chromatist Order[/b] - To them, the Tower is a [b]blessing[/b] - a wellspring of arcane wonders waiting to be mastered. They see the spreading corruption as a [b]temporary challenge[/b] to be overcome like any other. Their goal? [b]To harness its magick and wealth[/b] to elevate Goldwheat beyond its humble origins. Led by [b]noblemen and religious leaders[/b], they believe they have a divine duty to embrace the Tower’s power.
[/list]
[u][b][h2]Territory Control[/h2][/b][/u]
Every run matters. [b]As you clear the Tower of the Archmage's minions, discover its secrets and extract treasures[/b], your faction gains influence over different [b]modules of the Tower[/b]. 
[list]
[*] Territories controlled by your faction will provide [b]special bonuses[/b]. These may vary from hefty discounts and cheaper crafting costs to enhanced power and handy combat advantages.
[*] Despite their non-aggression treaty meant to protect the citizens of Goldwheat from unnecessary carnage, [b]Chromatists and Grey will still compete for control of the Tower[/b]! Specific territories are up for grabs and members of both factions will have to race to raise the most amount of influence and retain the disputed territories' bonuses so that they stand a chance at facing the Archmage's Lair and live to tell the tale.
[/list]
[u][b][h2]Drive the Archmage Back[/h2][/b][/u]
Deep within the Tower lies the Archmage’s Lairs, where his Chromatic Aberrations spread their twisted influence. Each conquered region brings your faction closer to these chaotic strongholds.
[list]
[*] [b]Corrupted Lairs[/b] – Expect [b]enhanced enemy mutations, unpredictable magic, and intense challenges[/b] as you push deeper. If left unchecked, [b]the Archmage’s forces can reclaim lost ground, undoing your faction’s progress![/b]
[*] [b]Defend your Home[/b] - The Archmage [b]will fight back[/b]. Both factions are subject to losing their conquered territories if they let the Lairs' raids reach them.
[/list]
[i](For this playtest, Lairs will be normal maps with additional mutators that make the game more difficult. In the near future, [b]Lairs will house raid bosses[/b] meant to be fought by parties of up to 10 players)[/i]

[u][b][h2]Write the Future of Goldwheat[/h2][/b][/u]
[b]Each season will shape the evolving story of Shadows of Chroma Tower[/b]. Your faction’s victory could determine new features, items, recipes, and enemies for future iterations.
[list]
[*] Will the Grey Fellowship succeed in purging the Tower’s corruption and returning Goldwheat to its prosperous past?
[*] Will the Chromatist Order master Chromatic Magick without succumbing to its influence, unveiling an entire new reality for all to see?
[/list]
The fate of Goldwheat is in your hands. Make your mark, and fight for your faction!

[i]PS: This playtest was originally meant to start on March 28th, but due to the complex nature of F&T, we decided it was best to postpone it by a week in order to deliver a more polished experience to our players. In good news, postponing it by a week also means we get to showcase some more new content throughout the playtest! Stay tuned for sneak peeks[/i]

notes.title: SNEAK PEEK: PROFESSIONS AND CRAFTING 🛠️
notes.content:
Crafting is half of our professions system, which fans of MMOs and ARPGs will likely be very familiar with. Leveling up a profession happens in parallel with your character's progression. You'll be able to dismantle items found within the tower and use the resulting materials to craft different items more suited to your class and playstyle.

By leveling up, crafting professions unlock better item rarities, new item archetypes and enchantments, while gathering professions gain better passive boosts to their baseline perks and new perks.

Characters always have access to all professions, but may only incorporate one of the gathering professions at a time within dungeons.


Here is our planned content for the FINAL version of this feature:
[h2]CRAFTING[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Forgemaster[/b] - Crafts general-use equipment such as weapons, armor, backpacks and accessories. Forgemasters are also able to enchant and reforge existing equipment in order to customize them to the player's needs.
[*] [b]Alchemist[/b] - Crafts Spellplates and Elixir Essences. Spellplates are combat-oriented consumables and elixir essences provide limited-use boosts to your Elixir. Only one elixir essence may be equipped at a time.
[*] [b]Cook[/b] - Crafts food-related items that can be consumed by a party before going into the dungeons to provide unique bonuses for the duration of the next match.
[/list]

[h2]GATHERING[/h2]

[h3]Miner[/h3]
[list]
      [*] Mines metals and gems with increased efficiency.
      [*] Mineral nodes show up on their minimap.
      [*] Can use their pickaxe to break down specific walls within the dungeons, revealing shortcuts and secret areas.
[/list]
[h3]Herbalist[/h3]
[list]
      [*] Finds herbs and vegetables within containers with increased efficiency.
      [*] Herbs and Vegetables containers show up on their minimap.
      [*] Can throw magical seeds on the ground that sprout into a temporary vine barrier, slowing down any characters that touch it.
[/list]
[h3]Survivalist[/h3]
[list]
      [*] Has increased chances of finding ‘crafting-loot’ within enemies’ corpses.
      [*] Harvests skin and meat from specific enemies’ corpses.
      [*] Can use a grappling hook to move around the map.
[/list]

At launch, the Forgemaster profession will include its core features, with enchanting and reforging planned for future updates. [i]Additional professions will be added over time as the game evolves.[/i]

What profession are you most excited to try out?

notes.title: 📢 Important Update on Shadows of Chroma Tower's Future
notes.content:
First off—thank you! Our recent playtest was [b]a massive success[/b], with almost 4,000 players diving into the game, giving feedback, and helping shape its future. Seeing so many of you play and discuss the game reinforced something important: Shadows of Chroma Tower has the [b]potential to be something truly special[/b].

Since Discord has a character limit on messages, we’re linking our [u][b][url=https://www.notion.so/doubledashstu/SoCT-Playtest-4a8220d745c3461d81a0f087c0e59cc4]Playtest Results[/url][/b][/u] page for those interested in checking out our analysis. Over the next couple of weeks, we’ll be fixing bugs, addressing balance issues, and implementing missing features based on your feedback. 

Today, we want to share a [u][b]MAJOR DECISION[/b][/u] about the game’s direction. [b]We know this won’t appeal to everyone, and it’s not a decision we’ve made lightly.[/b] With that in mind, [b]keep discussions respectful[/b], even if this change isn’t aligned with your personal taste. We are always open to feedback as long as it’s respectful.

[h2]❌ Shadows of Chroma Tower will no longer be PvPvE[/h2]
After careful analysis of the playtest data, community feedback, and our long-term goals, we’ve made the [b][u]difficult (but necessary) decision to remove PvP from dungeons.[/u] Shadows of Chroma Tower will now be a fully PvE-focused game.[/b] But we’re developing competitive features to maintain intensity and excitement.

[h2]❓ Why Are We Removing PvP?[/h2]
The short answer? Sustainability. We want SoCT to be an enjoyable game to play 5 years from now as much as it will be on release. We don't want to plan it in such a way that, if we end up with 100 daily users eventually, it becomes a barren shell of what it was in its launch week.

The long answer? PvP creates and catalyzes several major issues for a small studio with an even smaller budget such as ours:

[h2]1️⃣ The Population Problem (Critical Mass)[/h2]
[*]A [b]PvPvE game needs a consistently large player base[/b] to work. If lobbies aren’t full, PvP encounters feel rare, unfair, or frustrating.
[*]Without [b]tens of thousands of daily players, PvP won’t feel rewarding[/b], and players will leave due to long wait times or empty matches.
[*]In games like this, [b]if we fail to hit that "critical mass" of players, we don’t just disappoint one group of players—we disappoint all of them[/b] as we've seen happen to other games in the past:
[list]
      [*][b]PvPers[/b] get bored due to rare fights.
      [*][b]PvE players[/b] feel forced into PvP situations they didn’t want.
      [*][b]Social/exploration-focused players[/b] struggle to find trade or co-op partners.[/list]
[*]We have analyzed alternatives to our current approach to reduce population segmentation, and I do not have enough characters in this Discord Announcement to go through it. Suffice to say we'd need [b]MILLIONS of dollars to penetrate the market and guarantee we'd reach AND MAINTAIN critical mass population.[/b]
[*]I have read your suggestion threads and there's no silver bullet to this issue that is accessible to us as a studio and doesn't infringe our vision for the game. Your suggestions were not ignored and are very much appreciated.

[h2]2️⃣ The Cost & Technical Burden of PvP[/h2]
[*][b]PvP increases the cost of dedicated servers, anti-cheat, and backend:[/b] all of which are already expensive and difficult to maintain for a smaller studio.
[*][b]Balance costs:[/b] With our very limited team size and budget, PvP draws a lot of our game design and programming efforts to ensuring balance among all classes and viable builds.
[*][b]Development slows down:[/b] Every new skill, enemy, or system needs double the balancing and implementation effort.

[h2]3️⃣ The Gameplay Limitations under PvPvE[/h2]
[*]Level design is rigid to prevent unfair PvP fights, spawn rushing and other frustrating scenarios (and even while aware of these issues, solving them is difficult and requires many iterations to get right).
[*]PvE encounters have to be "toned down" to account for spontaneous PvP encounters.
[*]Creativity becomes limited by cost, since everything must be implemented for both PvP and PvE and designed with two very distinct crowds and gameplay styles in mind.
[*]The overarching game design becomes limited and we can't lean into a design that 100% satisfies either crowd. Adding a 5th difficulty, for instance, becomes unfeasible due to population segmentation, adding a new equipment rarity/tier becomes unfeasible due to gear/stat gaps, even more 'innocent' things such as character customization becomes limited (or at the very least more costly) because we need to make sure character classes are very easily distinguishable from one another in PvP encounters.

[h2]🔄 What This Means for Gameplay[/h2]
[*][b]Dungeons will now be purely PvE[/b], with a focus on [b]challenging, hand-crafted enemy encounters.[/b]
[*][b]Matchmaking remains co-op[/b], with [b]teams of up to 3 players[/b] tackling the dungeon together.
[*][b]More design freedom[/b], allowing for [b]bigger, more unique enemy types, class abilities, PvE mechanics, and maps[/b] that wouldn’t have been possible before.
[*][b]Faster Content Output[/b], since our team will have a lot less to worry about when designing content and it will be MUCH easier to iterate over developed content.
[*][b]Clearer Class Roles[/b], meaning we get a chance to fulfill our vision of sticking to more traditional RPG party roles - tank, support, DPS. And don't worry, all classes will be viable for solo gameplay.

[h2]✅ How We’re Keeping the Competitive Thrill Alive[/h2]
We know many of you love [b]competition[/b], so we’re shifting that focus towards [b]asynchronous and parallel competitive systems[/b], including:
[*][b]🏆 Leaderboards[/b] – Seasonal Leaderboards like the ones you saw during the January Playtest.
[*][b]🗺️ Factions & Territories (F&T)[/b] – A global war where players [b]conquer and defend territories[/b] while the Archmage’s forces fight back. Players may affiliate with one of the two factions and each conquered territory within the tower confers perks and bonuses to players of that faction. We have teased this feature in the past, but if you've missed the teaser, this is not too distinct from Helldivers 2's overarching metagame.
[*][b]🎮 Parallel-Play PvP[/b] - Together with the asynchronous PvP activities (leaderboards and F&T), we will introduce seasonal Parallel-Play PvP activities where there is no direct PvP encounter, but teams compete within the same match to win, being able to disrupt each other's gameplay in various ways. [b]If you have ever played [u]Hero Line Wars or Rabbits vs Sheep[/u][/b] in the old Warcraft 3 days, you might have an idea of what we're aiming for.
[*][b]⚔️ Post-Launch PvP Roadmap[/b] – Our future as a studio is hanging on the commercial performance of SoCT. If we achieve an initial success great enough to keep us afloat for another few months, we will dedicate a chunk of our efforts to making PvP gamemodes such as an Arena mode, or, if the success is great enough to mitigate all of the problems previously mentioned, even bring back opt-in PvP to dungeons.

[h2]💬 Let Us Know Your Thoughts[/h2]
This decision wasn’t made lightly, and we know it might be unexpected for some of you. However, we [b]strongly believe this is the best path forward[/b] for Shadows of Chroma Tower to thrive [b]long-term[/b].

We’d love to hear your thoughts, so feel free to use any of the discussion channels to express your feelings ([b]in a respectful way[/b]), and help us shape this game together.

Thank you for being part of this journey!

notes.title: SNEAK PEEK: REWORKED RANGED COMBAT MECHANICS 🏹
notes.content:
With the introduction of hordes and an emphasis on group combat, we want all classes to have single-target and multi-target/AoE damage-dealing options. We've been revisiting the Hunter's capacity of dealing with multiple enemies and decided to rework how the bow-and-arrow works.

Before, firing your bow would always shoot the same projectile no matter how long you drew the bow for - same speed, damage, everything. Now we've introduced the "[b]Charged Shot[/b]" and "[b]Power Shot[/b]" mechanics.
[list]
[*][b]Charged Shot[/b] - The longer you draw your arrow, the more powerful the shot will be, up to a limit. Drawing increases projectile damage, speed and adds penetrative power to it, allowing the ranger to consistently deal with lined-up targets.
[*][b]Power Shot[/b] - Upon charging a shot, releasing it at just the right time will shoot an even more powerful projectile. This will reward players with good mechanical dexterity and quick reflexes and will also help us balance the Hunter for multiple scenarios. 
[/list]
Both mechanics may vary from bow to bow as we introduce new features to the Hunter, such as elemental arrows and quivers.

The Hunter awaits you within the Tower!

notes.title: SNEAK PEEK: CHARACTER CUSTOMIZATION 🎩
notes.content:
Our character creation and customization system is almost ready! Letting players express themselves through their character is important to us, so here is a [b]preliminary[/b] list of customizable appearance features:
[list]
[*] Body type
[*] Hair and facial hair (color and style)
[*] Make-up, face paint and facial scars (color and style)
[*] Skin tone
[*] Eyes (color and style)
[/list]
Of course, that customization comes on top of all the different armor and weapon sets your character will be able to equip.
We also plan on having different base appearances for each class and hope to show you those new character meshes in the near future 🙂

Let us know what you think and if there's something else you'd like to customize on your character!

notes.title: THE ALPHA PLAYTEST STARTS JANUARY 31st!
notes.content:
Hello Guys! We are happy to announce, our Alpha Playtest begins on [b]January 31, 2025 at 8:00 PM (GMT-3)[/b].

[h3]DURATION[/h3]
The playtest servers will open for [b]48 hours[/b], closing on [b]Sunday, February 2, 2025 at 8:00 PM (GMT-3)[/b].

[h3]WHO WILL BE INVITED?[/h3]
We currently have over 5000 players signed up from all over the world. Due to budget limitations (servers cost a lot!), we're inviting only 4000 players with a very rough estimate that about half of the invitees will actually participate. We're prioritizing regions with the highest amount of players signed up, which means US and Canada in North America, Brazil in South America and Eastern Europe (Middle ground between Russia and Germany, which have the 4th and 5th most signed up players respectively).

[h3]I DIDN'T GET AN INVITE! WHAT NOW?[/h3]
Invites will be sent out next week. If you haven't been invited by then, send us a message send us a message on [url=https://discord.com/invite/84bgPFcPNj ]Discord[/url] or on our [url=https://www.twitch.tv/chromatower]Twitch channel[/url], since we'll probably be streaming during the playtest. If you're not in the mentioned regions, though, expect to play with a higher latency, which might not amount to the best experience possible.

[h3]WHAT ARE WE TESTING?[/h3] 
Players will have access to a Late Alpha build. At this point, the game is by no means feature complete, but has a playable vertical slice that includes a good chunk of its metagame (crafting, upgrades, vendors, leaderboards, etc) and a good chunk of its in-dungeon gameplay (combat, difficulties, classes, character building, etc).

Even though this is Alpha, we expect to deliver a smooth and polished experience to our players, even if it means we won't deliver a dungeon boss or a second level as quickly as we'd like. If your experience during this playtest does not match this, by all means send us feedback.

[previewyoutube=AOL94aFvJw0;full][/previewyoutube]

Below is a list of the new features that will be available for you to test and conquer! 
[list]
[*] [b]THE WEAVER[/b] :fireball: - Our first caster class. They steal flames, bonk heads and hurl fireballs.
[*] [strike]7 weapons[/strike] to [b]16 WEAPONS[/b] ⚔️ - We more than doubled the number of ways you can defeat your enemies.
[*] [strike]3 armor sets[/strike] to [b]8 ARMOR SETS[/b] 👕  - There's one for every playstyle.
[*] [strike]5 enemy types[/strike] to [b]8 ENEMY TYPES[/b] :enemy: - And there's a lot more of them, too! You're not getting away so easily this time 😉
[*] [b]NEW EQUIPMENT SLOT [/b]- Backpacks, Cloaks and Quivers so your back doesn't go unburdened.
[*][b] NEW MODULES[/b] - New map variants and modules to make sure you always have something new to find every run.
[*] [b]DIFFICULTIES[/b] - 4 difficulty levels to choose from, including PvE modes for newer players.
[*] [b]THE ELIXIR[/b] - No more bandages and health potions. The Elixir is your only way to recover missing health (for now!).
[*] [b]CHARACTER UPGRADES[/b] - Our precursor to skill trees, you'll upgrade your inventory space, minimap, elixir and many other capabilities using Soul Shards.
[*] [b]CRAFTING[/b] - Dismantle unwanted items and use their raw materials to make new ones. Level up your Forgemaster profession to unlock even better items.
[*] [b]LEADERBOARDS[/b] - Three distinct leaderboards for three distinct types of players. Rewards will be announced when the playtest starts.
[*] [b]HORDES AND CURSED CHESTS[/b] - You'll want to be properly prepared for these...
[*] [b]SAFE SLOTS[/b] - Because no one likes going in and out of a 15-minute match and having nothing to show for it.
[*] [b]REWORKED COMBAT AND ATTRIBUTES[/b] - You thought you knew how to build your character? Think again! Weapons now scale with primary attributes. Combat is now faster. You'll have to play to know what else has changed.
[*] [b]VOIP[/b] - It's a work in progress and it's there due to popular demand!
[*] [b]NEW GIRAFFE CHALLENGE[/b] - Well, sort of... You'll find very special rewards for finishing on top of the leaderboards and for achieving max level on your Forgemaster profession.
[/list]

notes.title: SNEAK PEEK: PLAYABLE CLASS - THE WEAVER 🔥
notes.content:
Hello, everyone! Here's a sneak peek [b]I KNOW[/b] you've been waiting for 😛

We’re introducing the Weaver, SoCT's first caster class. Weavers are scholars of Chromatic Magick that have learned to bend the elements of the Tower to their will and weave the leylines as they see fit.

In the January Playtest, Weavers will be limited to [b]manipulating fire[/b], conjuring flames to devastate enemies and control the battlefield. To unlock their full potential, players must be aware of nearby flame sources at all times, as Weavers [b]can absorb these flames to replenish their precious mana[/b]. You don't want to be caught unprepared and have to resort to [b]bonking heads with a staff. You're a scholar, not a barbarian![/b]

But fire is just the beginning. In future updates, you’ll be able to shape your Weaver through its skill tree, unlocking the ability to harness other kinds of Magick.

⚔️[b] Equipment[/b] (for the January Playtest):
[list]
[*] 🗡️ Daggers
[*] 🪄 Wands
[*] 🧙 Staves (each with their own unique spell)
[*] 👗 Cloth Armor
[*] 👕 Caster Armor
[*] 🎒 Backpacks, Cloaks, Rings and Amulets
[/list]

Let us know your thoughts and get ready to set the Tower ablaze! 🔥

notes.title: SNEAK PEEK: QUIVERS AND ITEM PERKS 🏹
notes.content:
Hello, everyone! I hope you've all had a fantastic holiday season and wish you an amazing 2025!

We've been working hard to deliver the best possible experience for our next playtest on [b]January 31st[/b] (we'll have a proper announcement about it soon :P). One of the features we are particularly excited about is [b]Item Perks[/b]!

To demonstrate a small fraction of what Item Perks are, here's a video showing off the [b]Ice and Fire Quivers[/b]. They're backslot items - like Cloaks and Backpacks - that allow Hunters to deal some magical damage while applying ailments to their target.

But that's not all! These quivers also open way for some tactical gameplay, allowing Hunters to [b]synergize with allied Weavers[/b] by igniting flame sources with their Fire Arrows, or to [b]disrupt enemy Weavers' gameplay[/b] by putting out their flame sources. We haven't fully unveiled the Weaver class yet, but think of them as Fire Mages that rely heavily on manipulating fire sources for now. 

Let us know your thoughts and see you soon!

notes.title: 🧙‍♂️SNEAK PEEK: THE SUMMONER has joined the Archmage's roster!
notes.content:
Hello, adventurers! Summoners serve as conduits for the Archmage's will throughout the Chroma Tower, ensuring that lesser minions perform their duties effectively in the tower's most crucial areas.

While all minions are essentially empty husks controlled by the Archmage's curse, Summoners retain a glimmer of their former selves. Observant adventurers may notice them whispering among themselves and exhibiting a level of intelligence that sets them apart from other minions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45049466/b265e9df8bf5727d221f00707cc004dc4572be9f.gif[/img]

As ranged combatants, Summoners invoke Kobolds and unleash magical projectiles infused with Chromatic Magick upon their foes. When cornered, they can swiftly teleport away from danger, only to resume their barrage from a safer distance.

[i]The Summoners await you within the Tower. [/i]😉 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45049466/f91ebc71eb173fd38a0f5da8bf53a513988d17af.png[/img]

notes.title: SNEAK PEEK: CURSED CHESTS! ✨
notes.content:
Hello, adventurers! Today we're showcasing a new feature in [i]Shadows of Chroma Tower[/i]: [b]Cursed Chests![/b]
These chests present an optional challenge for our more seasoned adventurers, for before you can claim their treasures, you must first lift their curse. Each cursed chest triggers an objective-based event, and upon completing the task, the curse will be lifted, granting you access to the loot inside.

Expect a variety of objectives, ranging from combat encounters to mind-bending puzzles. In the video below, you’ll see a wave-survival-style event in action.

Hope you enjoy our new feature! 😄
